questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct statement?
options: Acetone undergoes reaction in presence of Ba(OH)_2$ on heating to form 4–Methylpent–3–en–2–one$
Acetophenone cannot be prepared on reacting Benzoyl chloride with Dimethyl cadmium in ether solvent
Acetophenone on reaction with I_2$ / Na_2$ CO_3$ (aq) does not undergo any reaction due to the presence of deactivating $-$COCH_3$ group
Acetone reacts with NH_2-$NH_2$ / KOH in Glycol on heating to form the saturated hydrocarbon, Butane
questions.solution:
Acetone (C$H_3$ COCH_3$) undergoes aldol condensation in the presence of a base like Ba(OH)_2$. Two molecules of acetone condense to form diacetone alcohol, which upon heating loses a water molecule to form an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone. \\ \\ 2 CH_3$ COCH_3\xrightarrow{\text{Ba(OH)}_2}$ (CH_3$)_2$ C(OH)CH_2$ COCH_3\xrightarrow{\Delta}$ (CH_3$)_2$ C=CHCOCH_3$ + H_2$ O \\ \\ The IUPAC name of the product (CH_3$)_2$ C=CHCOCH_3$ is 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one (commonly known as mesityl oxide). Thus, statement (A) is correct.

For the other options:
Statement (B) is incorrect because acetophenone (PhCOCH_3$) can be prepared by the reaction of benzoyl chloride (PhCOCl) with dimethyl cadmium ((CH_3$)_2$ Cd). \\ \\ Statement (C) is incorrect because acetophenone contains a methyl ketone group ($-$COCH_3$) and gives a positive iodoform test with I_2$ and a base (like Na_2$ CO_3$), forming a yellow precipitate of CHI_3$.

Statement (D) is incorrect because the Wolff-Kishner reduction (NH_2$ NH_2$ / KOH in glycol) of acetone (a 3-carbon compound) yields propane, not butane.

Answer: Acetone undergoes reaction in presence of Ba(OH)_2$ on heating to form 4–Methylpent–3–en–2–one

W$C_6H_5CH_3 \xrightarrow{\large{(i)CrO_3 + (CH_3CO)_2O;\ (ii)H_2O + heat}}$P$R_2CO$

options: W - R X - P Y - Q Z - S
W - Q X - P Y - S Z - R
W - S X - R Y - Q Z - P
W - R X - S Y - P Z - Q
questions.solution:
Reaction W: Toluene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_3$) reacts with chromic oxide ($\text{CrO}_3$) in acetic anhydride to form benzylidene diacetate, which on hydrolysis yields benzaldehyde ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$). Thus, W matches with R.

Reaction X: Esters ($\text{RCOOC}_2\text{H}_5$) are reduced by DIBAL-H to aldehydes ($\text{RCHO}$). Thus, X matches with S.

Reaction Y: Nitriles ($\text{RCN}$) react with Grignard reagents ($\text{RMgX}$) to form an imine complex, which upon acid hydrolysis yields a ketone ($\text{R}_2\text{CO}$). Thus, Y matches with P.

Reaction Z: Acid chlorides ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCl}$) react with dialkylcadmium ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{Cd}$) to form ketones. Here, benzoyl chloride reacts with dimethylcadmium to form acetophenone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$). Thus, Z matches with Q.

The correct matching is W - R, X - S, Y - P, Z - Q.

Answer: W - R X - S Y - P Z - Q

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify products [P$_1$] and [P$_2$] formed when Benzonitrile undergoes the following reactions.
questions.solution:
1. Formation of [X]: Benzonitrile ($C_6H_5CN$) undergoes Stephen reduction when treated with $SnCl_2/HCl$ in ether, forming an imine intermediate. Subsequent acid hydrolysis ($H_3O^+$) yields benzaldehyde ($C_6H_5CHO$). Thus, [X] is benzaldehyde.

2. Formation of [P$_1$]: Benzaldehyde reacts with $HCN$ to undergo nucleophilic addition, forming benzaldehyde cyanohydrin ($C_6H_5CH(OH)CN$). Acid hydrolysis ($H_3O^+$) of the nitrile group converts it into a carboxylic acid group, yielding $\alpha$-hydroxy phenylacetic acid ($C_6H_5CH(OH)COOH$). Thus, [P$_1$] is $\alpha$-hydroxy phenylacetic acid.

3. Formation of [P$_2$]: Benzaldehyde does not have any $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms. When treated with a concentrated base ($50\%\ NaOH$), it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction (a disproportionation reaction). Two moles of benzaldehyde react to form one mole of benzyl alcohol ($C_6H_5CH_2OH$) and one mole of sodium benzoate ($C_6H_5COO^-Na^+$), which is the salt. Thus, [P$_2$] is benzyl alcohol.

Answer: [P$_1$] $\alpha$–Hydroxy phenylacetic acid and [P$_2$] Benzyl alcohol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT TRUE about nucleophilic addition reactions of aldehydes?
options: The hydrogensulphite addition product is useful for separation and purification of aldehydes
Aldehydes and ketones react very slowly with pure HCN to yield cyanohydrins
2,4 DNP derivatives are useful to identify aldehydes and ketones
questions.solution:
Hemiacetals contain one alkoxy group ($-OR$) and one hydroxyl group ($-OH$) attached to the same carbon atom. They are gem-alkoxyalcohols. Acetals contain two alkoxy groups attached to the same carbon atom and are known as gem-dialkoxy compounds. Thus, the statement that hemiacetals are gem-dialkoxy compounds is incorrect.

The sodium bisulphite addition product is crystalline and water-soluble, and can be converted back to the original carbonyl compound by treating it with dilute mineral acid or alkali. Therefore, it is useful for the separation and purification of aldehydes.

Pure $HCN$ reacts very slowly with aldehydes and ketones because it is a weak acid and generates cyanide ions very slowly. The reaction is typically catalyzed by a base.

2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazine reacts with aldehydes and ketones to form 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazones, which are usually yellow, orange, or red solids, making them useful for characterization.

Answer: Hemiacetals are gem-dialkoxy compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Propanal on reaction with dilute NaOH, undergoes aldol condensation resulting in the formation of a compound A. Identify the correct structure of A and name of the compound.
questions.solution:
Propanal (CH_3-CH_2-CHO$) undergoes self-aldol condensation in the presence of dilute NaOH.

The \alpha$-carbon of one propanal molecule is deprotonated by the base to form an enolate ion:
$CH_3-CH_2-CHO + OH^- \rightleftharpoons CH_3-\bar{C}H-CHO + H_2O$

This enolate ion acts as a nucleophile and attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon of a second propanal molecule:
$CH_3-CH_2-CHO + CH_3-\bar{C}H-CHO \rightarrow CH_3-CH_2-CH(O^-)-CH(CH_3)-CHO$

Protonation of the resulting alkoxide ion from water yields the aldol product (Compound A):
$CH_3-CH_2-CH(O^-)-CH(CH_3)-CHO + H_2O \rightarrow CH_3-CH_2-CH(OH)-CH(CH_3)-CHO + OH^-$

To name this compound according to IUPAC rules, we select the longest carbon chain containing the aldehyde group, which has 5 carbon atoms (pentanal). Numbering starts from the aldehyde carbon:
C1: $-CHO$
C2: $-CH(CH_3)-$
C3: $-CH(OH)-$
C4: $-CH_2-$
C5: $-CH_3$

There is a methyl group at C2 and a hydroxy group at C3. Thus, the IUPAC name is 3-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal. This matches the structure and name given in option (D).

Answer: 3-hydroxy-2-methyl-pentanal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Etard reaction is a method of preparation of benzaldehyde by oxidation of toluene. The oxidizing agent used in this reaction is:
questions.solution:
The Etard reaction involves the oxidation of toluene to benzaldehyde.

The oxidizing agent used in this reaction is chromyl chloride (CrO_2Cl_2$) dissolved in a non-polar solvent such as $CS_2$ or $CCl_4$.

The reaction proceeds via the formation of a brown chromium complex, which upon hydrolysis yields benzaldehyde.

Answer: Chromyl chloride$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds will not give Iodoform reaction?
questions.solution:
The iodoform test is given by compounds containing the $CH_{3}CO-$ group or the $CH_{3}CH(OH)-$ group.

Ethanol is $CH_{3}CH_{2}OH$, which contains the $CH_{3}CH(OH)-$ group. It gives a positive iodoform test.

Isobutyl alcohol is $(CH_{3})_{2}CHCH_{2}OH$. This structure does not contain the $CH_{3}CH(OH)-$ group. Therefore, it does not give the iodoform reaction.

3-methyl-2-butanone is $CH_{3}COCH(CH_{3})_{2}$, which contains the $CH_{3}CO-$ group. It gives a positive iodoform test.

Propan-2-ol is $CH_{3}CH(OH)CH_{3}$, which contains the $CH_{3}CH(OH)-$ group. It gives a positive iodoform test.

Answer: Isobutyl alcohol

Answer: Isobutyl alcohol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Aldol condensation reaction between which of the following pair of compounds followed by dehydration gives 3-phenylprop-2-en-1-al?
questions.solution:
The target product is 3-phenylprop-2-en-1-al, which has the structure $C_{6}H_{5}-CH=CH-CHO$.

This compound is an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated aldehyde. Aldol condensation between an aldehyde containing an $\alpha$-hydrogen and another carbonyl compound followed by dehydration typically yields such products.

The structure $C_{6}H_{5}-CH=CH-CHO$ can be retrosynthetically broken down at the double bond into benzaldehyde (C_{6}H_{5}CHO$) and acetaldehyde (CH_{3}CHO$).

The reaction proceeds as follows: Benzaldehyde (C_{6}H_{5}CHO$) reacts with acetaldehyde (CH_{3}CHO$) in the presence of a dilute base. Acetaldehyde provides the $\alpha$-hydrogen to form an enolate, which attacks the carbonyl carbon of benzaldehyde to form 3-hydroxy-3-phenylpropanal. Subsequent dehydration of this aldol product yields 3-phenylprop-2-en-1-al (cinnamaldehyde).

Answer: Benzaldehyde and Acetaldehyde

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of their reactivity in nucleophilic addition reactions. p-nitrobenzaldehyde (I); methylphenylketone (II); benzaldehyde (III); 4-methylbenzaldehyde (IV)
questions.solution:
The reactivity of carbonyl compounds towards nucleophilic addition reactions is governed by two factors: steric hindrance and electronic effects. Steric hindrance decreases reactivity, while electron-withdrawing groups (EWG) increase reactivity by increasing the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon, and electron-donating groups (EDG) decrease reactivity.

The compounds are: (I) p-nitrobenzaldehyde, (II) methylphenylketone (acetophenone), (III) benzaldehyde, (IV) 4-methylbenzaldehyde.

Comparing the aldehydes (I, III, IV): p-nitrobenzaldehyde (I) has a strong EWG ($-NO_2$), making the carbonyl carbon highly electrophilic. Benzaldehyde (III) has no substituent. 4-methylbenzaldehyde (IV) has a methyl group, which is an EDG (+I and hyperconjugation), reducing the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon. Thus, the order for aldehydes is IV < III < I.

Comparing ketones and aldehydes: Methylphenylketone (II) is a ketone, which is less reactive than aldehydes due to both steric hindrance and the +I effect of the methyl group. Therefore, II is the least reactive among the given compounds.

Combining these, the increasing order of reactivity is II < IV < III < I.

Answer: II $ <$ IV $ <$ III $ <$ I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An organic compound "A" reacts with $\mathrm{Zn} / \mathrm{Hg} /$ Conc. HCl to form p-Xylene. It reduces Tollen's reagent and on oxidation with $\mathrm{KMnO}_4 / \mathrmH^{+}$ it yields 1, 4-benzenedicarboxylic acid.
Identify compound A.
questions.solution:
The compound A reacts with $\mathrm{Zn/Hg/Conc. HCl}$ (Clemmensen reduction) to form p-Xylene. This indicates that the carbonyl group of an aldehyde or ketone is reduced to a methylene group. The structure of p-Xylene is $1,4$-dimethylbenzene.

The compound A reduces Tollen's reagent, which is a characteristic test for aldehydes. Therefore, A must be an aldehyde.

Oxidation of A with $\mathrm{KMnO}_4/\mathrmH^{+}$ yields $1,4$-benzenedicarboxylic acid (terephthalic acid). This confirms that A has two substituents at the para positions, one of which is an aldehyde group (which oxidizes to a carboxylic acid) and the other is a methyl group (which oxidizes to a carboxylic acid).

Combining these observations, the structure of A is $4$-methylbenzaldehyde (p-methylbenzaldehyde). The aldehyde group at the para position is reduced to a methyl group by Clemmensen reduction to yield p-Xylene, and the aldehyde group is oxidized to a carboxylic acid while the methyl group is also oxidized to a carboxylic acid by $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$.

Answer: p-methylbenzaldehyde.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement.
options: Acetone undergoes Wolff Kishner reaction to yield Propane.

The increasing order of boiling points of 5 compounds having comparable molar masses is as follows:
Methoxyethane \(< \) Propanone \(< \) Propanal \(< \) Propan-1-ol
The order of reactivity towards Nucleophilic attack is Methanal > Ethanal > Benzaldehyde > Acetophenone
During nucleophilic addition of HCN to RCHO , the hybridisation changes from $\mathrm{sp}^2$ to $\mathrm{sp}^3$ and a tetrahedral intermediate is formed.
questions.solution:
Statement (2) is incorrect because ketones have higher boiling points than isomeric aldehydes due to greater dipole-dipole interactions from two electron-donating alkyl groups. Propanone (b.p. $\approx 56°C$) boils higher than Propanal (b.p. $\approx 49°C$).

The correct increasing order of boiling points should be:
Methoxyethane < Propanal < Propanone < Propan-1-ol

The given order in statement (2) places Propanone before Propanal, which is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the Carbonyl compound which will not be formed when hydration of Alkynes is carried out with dil. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4 / \mathrm{Hg}^{2+}$ at 333 K.
Acetone, Butanal, Ethanal, Butanone.
questions.solution:
Hydration of alkynes in the presence of dil. $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ and $\mathrm{Hg}^{2+}$ follows Markovnikov addition of water to the triple bond, forming an enol intermediate which tautomerizes to a carbonyl compound.

For ethyne (HC \equiv CH$), hydration yields ethenol, which tautomerizes to ethanal (CH_{3}CHO$).

For propyne (CH_{3}C \equiv CH$), hydration yields prop-1-en-2-ol, which tautomerizes to acetone (CH_{3}COCH_{3}$).

For but-1-yne (CH_{3}CH_{2}C \equiv CH$), hydration yields but-1-en-2-ol, which tautomerizes to butanone (CH_{3}COCH_{2}CH_{3}$).

For but-2-yne (CH_{3}C \equiv CCH_{3}$), hydration yields but-2-en-2-ol, which tautomerizes to butanone (CH_{3}COCH_{2}CH_{3}$).

Butanal (CH_{3}CH_{2}CH_{2}CHO$) is an aldehyde with four carbon atoms. It would require the anti-Markovnikov addition of water to but-1-yne or the hydration of a terminal alkyne at the terminal carbon, which is not the product of the acid-catalyzed hydration of alkynes using \mathrm{Hg}^{2+}$ catalyst. Therefore, butanal is not formed.

Answer: Butanal

questions.q: Identify $\mathrm{X}, \mathrm{Y}$ and Z formed in the reaction:

The starting material is 4-formylcyclohexanone.

Reaction with $\text{Zn/Hg}$ and $\text{conc. HCl}$ is the Clemmensen reduction, which reduces both the ketone and the aldehyde groups to methylene groups. Thus, Z is 1-methyl-4-methylcyclohexane, which is simply 1,4-dimethylcyclohexane.

Reaction with $\text{Cu}^{+2}/\text{OH}^{-}$ (Fehling's solution or similar oxidizing conditions) selectively oxidizes the aldehyde group to a carboxylic acid group, while the ketone remains unaffected. Subsequent acidification with $\text{H}_3\textO^{+}$ gives 4-oxocyclohexanecarboxylic acid as X.

Reaction of X with $\text{NaBH}_4$ reduces the ketone group to a secondary alcohol, while the carboxylic acid group remains unaffected. Thus, Y is 4-hydroxycyclohexanecarboxylic acid.

Comparing these structures with the given options, the first option (yNO2a) correctly identifies X as 4-oxocyclohexanecarboxylic acid, Y as 4-hydroxycyclohexanecarboxylic acid, and Z as 1,4-dimethylcyclohexane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify [ X ], the final product formed when 2 moles of Ethanal undergoes the following series of reactions with reagents [(i) to (iv)]
$\underset{2 \text{ moles }}{\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CHO}} \xrightarrow[\text{ (iii). } \mathrm{NaBH}_4 \text{ (iv). } \dfrac{C r_2 O_7^{2-}}{H^{+}}]{\text{(i). dil } \mathrm{NaOH} \text{ (ii) Heat. }}[\mathrm{X}]$
questions.solution:
The reaction of 2 moles of ethanal with dil. $\mathrm{NaOH}$ is an aldol condensation reaction. The two molecules of $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CHO}$ undergo condensation to form 3-hydroxybutanal: $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CHO} + \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{dil. NaOH}} \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH(OH)CH}_2\mathrm{CHO}$.

Heating 3-hydroxybutanal leads to dehydration via the E1cB mechanism, resulting in the formation of an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated aldehyde, which is but-2-enal (crotonaldehyde): $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH(OH)CH}_2\mathrm{CHO} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH=CHCHO} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$.

The reagent $\mathrm{NaBH}_4$ is a selective reducing agent that reduces the aldehyde group to a primary alcohol while leaving the carbon-carbon double bond intact: $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH=CHCHO} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{NaBH}_4} \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH=CHCH}_2\mathrm{OH}$ (but-2-en-1-ol).

Finally, the oxidation of the primary alcohol using $\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}/\mathrmH^{+}$ (Jones oxidation or similar strong oxidizing conditions) converts the primary alcohol group to a carboxylic acid group, yielding but-2-enoic acid: $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH=CHCH}_2\mathrm{OH} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}/\mathrmH^{+}} \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH=CHCOOH}$.

Answer: But-2-enoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound $[\mathrm{X}]$ reacts with $\mathrm{H}_2 / \mathrm{Pd}-\mathrm{BaSO}_4$ to give compound $[\mathrm{Y}]$ which reduces Tollen's reagent and undergoes Cannizzaro's reaction. On rigorous oxidation of [Y] in presence of $\mathrm{KMnO}_4 / \mathrmH^{+}$ Phthalic acid is the product obtained. What is $[\mathrm{X}]$ ?
questions.solution:
The reaction of an organic compound [X] with $H_{2}/Pd-BaSO_{4}$ (Rosenmund reduction) indicates that [X] is an acid chloride (R-COCl$).

The product [Y] obtained from this reduction is an aldehyde (R-CHO$).

Since [Y] reduces Tollen's reagent and undergoes Cannizzaro's reaction, [Y] must be an aromatic aldehyde (as it lacks $\alpha$-hydrogens).

Rigorous oxidation of [Y] with $KMnO_{4}/H^{+}$ yields phthalic acid. Phthalic acid is benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid. This implies that the starting material [X] must be an ortho-substituted benzene derivative with a $-COCl$ group and another group that can be oxidized to a $-COOH$ group at the ortho position.

The structure of phthalic acid is a benzene ring with two $-COOH$ groups at the 1 and 2 positions. Therefore, the precursor [Y] must be 2-methylbenzaldehyde (o-tolualdehyde), which upon oxidation gives phthalic acid. Consequently, the compound [X] must be 2-methylbenzoyl chloride.

Comparing this with the given options, the structure corresponding to 2-methylbenzoyl chloride is the one with a $-COCl$ group and a $-CH_{3}$ group at the ortho position.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two statements, one Assertion (A) and the other Reason (R) are given. Choose the correct option. Assertion: Compound $[\mathrm{X}]$ reacts with Hydrazine in presence of $\mathrm{KOH} /$ Glycol to form the product $[\mathrm{Y}]$.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both $A$ and $R$ are correct but $R$ is not the correct explanation of $A$.
A is wrong but R is correct.
questions.solution:
The reaction shown is the Wolff-Kishner reduction, which uses hydrazine (NH_{2}NH_{2}$) in the presence of a strong base like $KOH$ and a high-boiling solvent like ethylene glycol to reduce a carbonyl group (aldehyde or ketone) to a methylene group ($-CH_{2}-$).

In the given reaction, the aldehyde group ($-CHO$) in compound [X] is reduced to a methyl group ($-CH_{3}$) to form compound [Y].

The Wolff-Kishner reduction is specifically designed to reduce carbonyl compounds to alkanes. It does not affect other functional groups like alkyl halides under standard conditions, although strong bases like $KOH$ can potentially cause elimination reactions in alkyl halides. However, in the context of this transformation, the conversion of the aldehyde to the methyl group is the primary intended reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds undergo Aldol condensation followed by dehydration to give 3-phenylprop-2-en-1-al?
options:
Benzaldehyde and Acetone
Two molecules of Benzaldehyde
Benzaldehyde and Ethanal
Benzaldehyde and Acetophenone
questions.solution:
The target product is 3-phenylprop-2-en-1-al, which is cinnamaldehyde. Its structure is $C_{6}H_{5}-CH=CH-CHO$.

The structure contains a phenyl group attached to a three-carbon chain with an aldehyde functional group at the end. This indicates that the condensation occurs between an aromatic aldehyde (benzaldehyde) and an aliphatic aldehyde (ethanal).

The reaction is a Claisen-Schmidt condensation, a type of crossed aldol condensation. Benzaldehyde ($C_{6}H_{5}CHO$) acts as the electrophile because it lacks $\alpha$-hydrogens, and ethanal ($CH_{3}CHO$) acts as the nucleophile because it possesses $\alpha$-hydrogens.

The reaction proceeds as follows: $C_{6}H_{5}CHO + CH_{3}CHO \xrightarrow{OH^{-}} C_{6}H_{5}CH(OH)CH_{2}CHO \xrightarrow{-H_{2}O} C_{6}H_{5}CH=CHCHO$.

Therefore, the reactants are benzaldehyde and ethanal.

Answer: Benzaldehyde and Ethanal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the final product formed when Toluene undergoes a series of reactions with reagents given in the order:
(i) $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ / Sunlight
(ii) $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} / 373 \mathrm{ K}$
(iii) Acetophenone / $\mathrm{OH^-}$ at $293 \mathrm{ K}$
questions.solution:
Toluene reacts with $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ in the presence of sunlight to undergo free radical chlorination at the side chain, yielding benzal chloride, $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CHCl}_2$.

Hydrolysis of benzal chloride with $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ at $373 \mathrm{ K}$ replaces the two chlorine atoms with an oxygen atom to form benzaldehyde, $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CHO}$.

The reaction of benzaldehyde with acetophenone ($\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COCH}_3$) in the presence of a base ($\mathrm{OH}^{-}$) is a Claisen-Schmidt condensation reaction. This reaction involves the nucleophilic attack of the enolate ion of acetophenone on the carbonyl carbon of benzaldehyde, followed by dehydration to form an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone.

The product formed is $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CHCOC}_6\mathrm{H}_5$, which is 1,3-diphenylprop-2-en-1-one, commonly known as benzalacetophenone or chalcone.

Answer: 1, 3-Diphenylprop-2-en-1-one

questions.q: What is/are the product/s formed when Benzaldehyde and Ethanal react in presence of dil. $\mathrm{NaOH}$ followed by heating the intermediate product formed?
questions.solution:
The reaction between Benzaldehyde (C_{6}H_{5}CHO$) and Ethanal (CH_{3}CHO$) in the presence of dilute $NaOH$ is a crossed aldol condensation. Since Benzaldehyde has no $\alpha$-hydrogen, it acts as the electrophile, while Ethanal acts as the nucleophile.

The initial aldol addition product is $C_{6}H_{5}CH(OH)CH_{2}CHO$ (3-hydroxy-3-phenylpropanal). Upon heating, this undergoes dehydration to form 3-phenylprop-2-enal (cinnamaldehyde).

Additionally, Ethanal can undergo self-aldol condensation in the presence of dilute $NaOH$ to form $CH_{3}CH(OH)CH_{2}CHO$ (3-hydroxybutanal). Upon heating, this dehydrates to form but-2-enal (crotonaldehyde).

Therefore, the products formed are 3-phenylprop-2-enal and but-2-enal.

Answer: 3-Phenylprop-2-enal & But-2-enal

questions.q:
Given are the names of 4 compounds. Two of these compounds will not undergo Cannizzaro's reaction. Identify the two.
A. 2-Chlorobutanal
B. 2,2-Dimethylpropanal
C. Benzaldehyde
D. 2-Phenyl ethanol
questions.solution:
Cannizzaro reaction is a disproportionation reaction given by aldehydes that do not possess any $\alpha$-hydrogen atom. In the presence of a strong base, these aldehydes undergo self-oxidation and reduction to form a carboxylic acid salt and an alcohol.

Analyzing the given compounds:
A. 2-Chlorobutanal: The structure is $CH_3-CH_2-CHCl-CHO$. The carbon atom adjacent to the carbonyl group (the $\alpha$-carbon) has one hydrogen atom attached. Since it has an $\alpha$-hydrogen, it will undergo aldol condensation, not Cannizzaro reaction.

B. 2,2-Dimethylpropanal: The structure is $(CH_3)_3C-CHO$. The $\alpha$-carbon is bonded to three methyl groups and has no hydrogen atom attached. Therefore, it does not have an $\alpha$-hydrogen and will undergo Cannizzaro reaction.

C. Benzaldehyde: The structure is $C_6H_5-CHO$. The carbonyl carbon is attached directly to the benzene ring. There is no $\alpha$-hydrogen atom present. Therefore, it will undergo Cannizzaro reaction.

D. 2-Phenyl ethanol: The structure is $C_6H_5-CH_2-CH_2-OH$. This is a primary alcohol, not an aldehyde. Cannizzaro reaction is specific to aldehydes lacking $\alpha$-hydrogens. Thus, it will not undergo Cannizzaro reaction.

The compounds that will not undergo Cannizzaro reaction are 2-Chlorobutanal (A) and 2-Phenyl ethanol (D).

Answer: A & D

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect regarding acetal and ketal formation when Propanal and Propanone are separately reacted with Ethanol in presence of anhydrous $\mathrm{HCl}$ gas.
options: Rate of formation of acetal is greater than that of ketal formation.
Both Propanal and Propanone undergo Nucleophilic addition reaction during this process.
Propanal and Ethanol should be taken in the approximate ratio of $1: 2$ for acetal formation.
Anhydrous $\mathrm{HCl}$ gas decreases the electrophilicity of the Carbonyl Carbon.
questions.solution:
Propanal is an aldehyde and Propanone is a ketone. Aldehydes are more reactive towards nucleophilic addition than ketones due to both steric and electronic factors. Thus, the rate of acetal formation from propanal is greater than the rate of ketal formation from propanone.

Both reactions involve the nucleophilic attack of ethanol on the carbonyl carbon, which is a nucleophilic addition reaction.

Acetal formation is a reversible reaction. To shift the equilibrium towards the product (acetal), an excess of alcohol is typically used, or water is removed. The stoichiometric ratio for the reaction $RCHO + 2R'OH \rightarrow RCH(OR')_2 + H_2O$ is $1:2$.

Anhydrous $\mathrm{HCl}$ acts as an acid catalyst. It protonates the carbonyl oxygen, which increases the positive charge density on the carbonyl carbon, thereby increasing its electrophilicity and making it more susceptible to nucleophilic attack by ethanol. Therefore, the statement that $\mathrm{HCl}$ decreases the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon is incorrect.

Answer: Anhydrous $\mathrm{HCl}$ gas decreases the electrophilicity of the Carbonyl Carbon.

questions.q: A Carbonyl compound $\mathrm{X}$ when reacted with Methyl magnesium bromide followed by hydrolysis gave product $\mathrm{Y}$. When $\mathrm{Y}$ is heated with $\mathrm{Cu}$ at $573 \mathrm{ K}$, it gave $\mathrm{Z}$ (2- Methylbut-2-ene) as one of the products. Identify $\mathrm{X}$.
questions.solution:
The reaction of a carbonyl compound $\mathrm{X}$ with $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ followed by hydrolysis yields an alcohol $\mathrm{Y}$.

Heating alcohol $\mathrm{Y}$ with $\mathrm{Cu}$ at $573 \mathrm{ K}$ is a dehydrogenation reaction for primary and secondary alcohols, or a dehydration reaction for tertiary alcohols. Since the product $\mathrm{Z}$ is 2-methylbut-2-ene, which is an alkene, the reaction is a dehydration of a tertiary alcohol.

The structure of 2-methylbut-2-ene is $\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$.

The tertiary alcohol $\mathrm{Y}$ that dehydrates to form 2-methylbut-2-ene is 2-methylbutan-2-ol, which has the structure $\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})(\mathrm{CH}_{3})-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$.

The alcohol $\mathrm{Y}$ (2-methylbutan-2-ol) is formed by the reaction of a ketone with methylmagnesium bromide. Specifically, the reaction of butan-2-one ($\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$) with $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ followed by hydrolysis yields 2-methylbutan-2-ol.

Therefore, the carbonyl compound $\mathrm{X}$ is butan-2-one.

Answer: Butanone

Since 2,2-Dimethylbutanal has no $\alpha$-hydrogen, it cannot undergo Aldol condensation.

questions.q: What would be the products obtained when a mixture of p-Methoxy benzaldehyde and Methanal are heated with $50 \%$ concentrated Caustic soda solution?
options: p- Methoxy benzyl alcohol and methanol.
p- Methoxy sodium benzoate and sodium formate
p-Methoxy benzyl alcohol and sodium formate.
p- Methoxy sodium benzoate and sodium acetate.
questions.solution:
The reaction between p-Methoxybenzaldehyde and Methanal in the presence of concentrated aqueous sodium hydroxide (50% NaOH) is a crossed Cannizzaro reaction.

In a crossed Cannizzaro reaction involving an aromatic aldehyde and formaldehyde, formaldehyde acts as the reducing agent because it is more reactive towards nucleophilic attack by the hydroxide ion (OH^{-}$).

The mechanism involves the nucleophilic attack of $OH^{-}$ on the carbonyl carbon of formaldehyde to form a hydride donor species, which then transfers a hydride ion to the carbonyl carbon of p-Methoxybenzaldehyde.

Consequently, the formaldehyde is oxidized to sodium formate (HCOONa$), and the p-Methoxybenzaldehyde is reduced to p-Methoxybenzyl alcohol (CH_{3}OC_{6}H_{4}CH_{2}OH$).

The overall reaction is: $CH_{3}OC_{6}H_{4}CHO + HCHO + NaOH \rightarrow CH_{3}OC_{6}H_{4}CH_{2}OH + HCOONa$.

Answer: p-Methoxy benzyl alcohol and sodium formate.$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the organic compound which, on heating with strong solution of $\mathrm{NaOH}$, partly converted into an acid salt and partly into alcohol
questions.solution: Benzaldehyde lacks $\alpha-\mathrm{H}$ atom. On heating with strong $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution, it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction to produce benzoic acid and benzyl alcohol. Benzoic acid forms sodium salt with $\mathrm{NaOH}$.
